smt-2014-advanced-tiebreaker-01.title: Count the favourable colourings
smt-2014-advanced-tiebreaker-01.body:
There are $4^5=1024$ colourings. Exactly four nails of one colour: choose the colour (4), the odd nail (5 ways) and its different colour (3): $4\cdot5\cdot3=60$. All five the same: 4. Total $64$, so the probability is $\frac{64}{1024}=\frac1{16}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{16}$**

smt-2014-advanced-tiebreaker-02.title: Two forms
smt-2014-advanced-tiebreaker-02.body:
The sum of 16 consecutive integers starting at $a$ is $16a+120$, which is $\equiv8\pmod{16}$. The sum of 17 consecutive integers starting at $b$ is $17b+136=17(b+8)$, a multiple of 17 that is at least $17\cdot9=153$ (as $b\ge1$). Write it as $17k$; since $17\equiv1\pmod{16}$ we need $k\equiv8\pmod{16}$ with $k\ge9$. The smallest such $k$ is $24$, giving $408$. Check: $408=17\cdot 24=$ the sum of the 17 integers $16,\dots,32$, and $408=16\cdot18+120$ is the sum of the 16 integers $18,\dots,33$.

**Answer: 408**

smt-2014-advanced-tiebreaker-03.title: Symmetry
smt-2014-advanced-tiebreaker-03.body:
The process is equivalent to every guest first picking a distinct seat (a uniformly random assignment) and then sitting down in a uniformly random order. Look at the three guests: Alice and the two people whose seats are next to hers. Alice's two neighbours' seats are both occupied exactly when Alice is the last of these three to sit. By symmetry each of the three is equally likely to be last, so the probability is $\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**
